the effects of cell volume changes on efflux of the putative neurotransmitters GABA and taurine.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the -SH groups involved in the efflux of taurus are located on the cell membrane, whereas the -SH groups which regulate GABA efflux are probably associated with the cytoskeleton.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the efflux of GABA and taurine from brain cells is modulated by the redox state of the cell.
there is a role for SH groups in effluxes of taurus and GABA in the cerebral cortex and that the role of SH groups may be different in efflux of these two amino acids.
the effects of pCMPS on efflux are not due to the inhibition of a membrane-bound enzyme.
